item.title: Air Force and Space Force push for scale as supply-chain constraints persist
item.description: NATIONAL HARBOR, Md. — “Scaling” has become a watchword for Air Force and Space Force leaders as they push to field more weapons and space capabilities faster and in greater numbers.

item.title: More satellites watch the battlefield, putting a premium on making sense of the data
item.description: Space Force programs are tapping satellite data and AI to get intelligence to military commanders faster

item.title: Space Force chief says Iran war shows service’s expanding combat role
item.description: NATIONAL HARBOR, Md. — The U.S. Space Force played a direct combat role in the war with Iran, with guardians conducting electromagnetic warfare against an adversary in addition to providing satellite communications, navigation and missile warning to U.S. forces, the service’s top general said Sept 15.

item.title: Vega launches two Earth science satellites
item.description: PARIS — A Vega C rocket successfully launched a pair of Earth observation satellites for the European Space Agency and the European Commission on Sept. 14.

item.title: Critical design review cleared for 2027 in-orbit cubesat inspection demo
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — British startup Shield Space has completed the critical design review for Broadsword, a 2027 mission aiming to demonstrate satellite-inspection capabilities that defense customers could have in orbit within nine months of contract signing.

item.title: Companies defend Bromo joint venture
item.description: PARIS — Executives with the three European companies seeking to combine their space businesses say the merger is still needed even as European government funding increases.

item.title: SES and Elveo Mobile plan European D2D satellite factory
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — SES outlined plans Sept. 15 to establish direct-to-device satellite production capabilities in Europe with Elveo Mobile, aiming to build out a regional supply chain to expand the D2D operator’s low Earth orbit (LEO) constellation.

item.title: HawkEye 360 addresses sovereign demand with European entity and partners
item.description: PARIS – HawkEye 360 is addressing growing demand for sovereign space capabilities by establishing a European subsidiary, working with Leonardo to provide radio-frequency sensing to European customers and collaborating with ERA, part of the Czech Republic’s Omnipol Group, the company announced Sept. 15.

item.title: Iceye’s global presence expands to address sovereign demand
item.description: Since raising more than $1 billion in a Series F funding round, Iceye has moved rapidly to address growing demand for sovereign space capabilities. In quick succession, the Finnish synthetic […]

item.title: Sept. 21: What Comes Next for On-Orbit Servicing?
item.description: Join us for conversations about the tech, policies and business models required to build a functioning in-orbit logistics ecosystem

item.title: Space’s growing billion-dollar club
item.description: Download our new mapping of every private space company valued at $1 billion or more.

item.title: U.S. has deployed space-control weapons in orbit, Air Force secretary says
item.description: NATIONAL HARBOR, Md. — U.S. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink on Monday revealed that the United States has deployed space-control weapons in orbit, while also disclosing new milestones for military satellite programs tied to missile defense and long-range targeting.

item.title: U.S. allies commit $302 million to complete funding for Space Force communications satellite
item.description: NATIONAL HARBOR, Md. — Ten U.S. allies have agreed to provide $302 million to cover launch, ground-system upgrades and operations for the U.S. Space Force’s next Wideband Global SATCOM satellite, completing a funding plan for the Boeing-built military communications spacecraft.

item.title: Open Cosmos reaches unicorn status with $348 million funding round
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — Open Cosmos has raised 300 million euros ($348 million) to expand production facilities and upgrade its space-based intelligence and connectivity services, the British small satellite specialist announced Sept. 14.

item.title: You cannot task a changing planet
item.description: Every satellite tasking request begins with an assumption: Someone already knows where to look.

item.title: ColliMate demonstrates autonomous satcom orchestration software in orbit
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — ColliMate Space has demonstrated its Nexus software for autonomously managing satellite downlinks onboard a spacecraft for the first time, the Silicon Valley startup announced Sept. 14

item.title: HEO demonstrates close inspection through rendezvous and proximity operations
item.description: PARIS – HEO, the Australian company non-Earth imagery company, announced Sept. 14 how it repurposed an Earth-observation satellite to conduct close-range inspection of a Chinese Long March 2C rocket.

item.title: Satellogic to expand constellation with October launch
item.description: PARIS – Satellogic announced plans Sept. 14 to launch one NewSat Mark V and two NewSat Mark VI Earth-observation satellite in October.

item.title: Satellogic to launch six more Earth-observation satellites for Office of Naval Research Slingshot III program
item.description: PARIS – Satellogic announced an agreement Sept. 14 with Innovative Defense Technologies to launch six additional Earth-observation satellites for the U.S. Office of Naval Research Slingshot III program.

item.title: Exolaunch secures additional rideshare launches
item.description: PARIS — Launch services provider Exolaunch said Sept. 14 it secured capacity for rideshare payloads on two launches, including a flight on a Japanese rocket.

item.title: U.S. Air Force awards Antares $161 million to advance nuclear reactor for space
item.description: WASHINGTON — The nuclear microreactor startup Antares won a $161 million Department of the Air Force contract to develop and demonstrate a nuclear reactor for spacecraft.

item.title: Pentagon seeks AI to turn space, missile data into decisions within seconds
item.description: WASHINGTON — The Pentagon is seeking an artificial intelligence system capable of turning a flood of space, missile and intelligence data into operational threat assessments within seconds, a demanding application that would move commercial AI closer to the military decision-making loop.

item.title: Europe uses space summit to advocate for greater autonomy
item.description: PARIS — European officials used an international space conference to bolster the continent’s own space capabilities as they push for greater autonomy.

item.title: Startups seek to demonstrate 3D printing in vacuum of space
item.description: PARIS – Poland’s Orbital Matter and Dcubed of Germany are conducting on-orbit demonstrations of 3D printing in cubesats, a step toward creating solar arrays with additively manufactured booms. Orbital Matter […]

item.title: Apex to set up US D2D satellite manufacturing facility for Elveo Mobile
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — Apex is helping establish a dedicated factory in the United States to churn out direct-to-device satellites for Elveo Mobile, the D2D operator recently formed by the merger of Lynk Global and Omnispace.

item.title: BlackSky shares first-light imagery from fifth Gen3 satellite
item.description: PARIS — BlackSky Technology announced Sept. 14 that it collected and processed first light imagery from its fifth Gen3 satellite in less than 20 hours after liftoff on a Rocket Lab Electron rocket.

item.title: Sophia Space and SLI agree on $300 million financing for 10-satellite edge-computing constellation
item.description: PARIS – Sophia Space and aerospace leasing specialist SLI announced a $300 million financing framework Sept. 14 for a 10-satellite edge-computing constellation. Under the agreement, SLI will purchase satellites ​from […]

item.title: NASA offers details about, and defends, proposed space academy
item.description: PARIS — NASA has disclosed new details about a proposal to create a national space academy as the agency’s administrator defends the concept against criticism.

item.title: Summit declarations avoid controversy but fail to earn key endorsements
item.description: PARIS — Three declarations signed by dozens of countries at the International Space Summit largely avoided controversial positions but still failed to win support from some of the biggest space powers.

item.title: NOAA contract signals sharp increase in commercial weather data purchases
item.description: PARIS – The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration announced significant expansion of its commercial satellite data program with the Sept. 10 award of an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract to 14 companies.
